items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: But we met a nice young couple who was planning to get married soon, Hildchen and Gunter Kwiatkowsky, who invited us in their parents' home

ctx.x: The most that ever came to the joint was one Saturday when there were at least 150 of them at 11 o'clock. At 2'30, the waiters had chased them all away, except a couple of fellows at the bar. At 8p.m. when we went to work, the sun was still shinning, and when we finished at 4.a.m., day was breaking, and the only happy things living seemed to be birds that we heard singing. No one ever came to me and told me that they were jazz fans, and I know there were some in town because was a place not far from where I was…

But we met a nice young couple who was planning to get married soon, Hildchen and Gunter Kwiatkowsky, who invited us in their parents' home and also introduced us to some of their friends. Sometimes, we were invited by some of them or went out in some keller. Colgone had been very heavily bombed and it was quite a sad sight to see.

Nearly every afternoon, I and some of the other musicians would meet Bishop, Sammy and some of the German musicians at a sidewalk café where we would talk some trash as all cats do when they get together, and one day,Bishop told me a story about Sammy concerning his getting high on a certain German made cigarette. The way Bishop told the tale, it seems that Sammy liked to pick up on some gage now and then, but for a certain time, he had not been able to find the stuff.
